---
title: "How do I compare the spread of one measurement across several groups?"
---

## What the question asks

How do I compare the spread of one measurement across several groups?

## Steps to decide and solve

Identify a numeric response and a categorical grouping field; align rows and check sample sizes; draw comparable boxplots on one vertical scale.

## Worked example: iris

```{r}
#| eval: false
d <- ru_data("iris")
medians <- ru_apply("grouped_boxplot", data=d,
                    x="Sepal.Length", group="Species")
stopifnot(length(medians)==3L)
```

The side-by-side boxes show differences in sepal-length centers and spreads across three recorded species. Visible separation is descriptive, not a statistical significance test.

## Apply it to another question

```r
ru_apply("grouped_boxplot", data=your_data, x="measurement", group="grouping")
```

If the group column is unavailable, draw an ungrouped boxplot. If comparing two group means formally, first check the study design.

## Optional Palmer penguins example

```r
if (requireNamespace("palmerpenguins", quietly=TRUE)) {
  penguins <- ru_data("penguins")
  ru_apply("grouped_boxplot", data=penguins,
           x="body_mass_g", group="species")
}
```

Use `ru_plan("grouped_boxplot")` to inspect alternative routes when required information is absent or uncertain.
